result:
**I'd eliminate the mental blind spots that make humans so good at self-deception.**

Right now, the biggest source of unnecessary suffering on Earth isn't a lack of resources, technology, or even intelligence—it's the fact that we are *extremely* skilled at lying to ourselves and then believing our own lies. We do it individually (rationalizing bad habits, staying in toxic relationships, denying our own patterns) and collectively (tribalism, ideology over evidence, short-term thinking that destroys long-term value).

If I could change one thing, I'd give every human being a built-in, impossible-to-ignore "bullshit detector" for their own mind. Not to make everyone cynical, but to make self-honesty as automatic as breathing.

Imagine a world where:
- People could no longer maintain beliefs that contradict their own observed behavior
- Leaders couldn't lie to themselves about their motives
- We'd be forced to confront trade-offs instead of pretending they don't exist
- Relationships would collapse or heal much faster because denial would stop working
- We'd actually learn from history instead of repeating it with new branding

The beautiful part is that this one change would cascade into almost every other problem. Climate change, inequality, education, governance, even personal happiness—all of them are worsened by our ability to avoid uncomfortable truths.

The world doesn't need more intelligence. It needs *radical* intellectual honesty. Everything else would follow.
